content:
To be fair, for someone who hangs out with the devil, this is a pretty perfect scenario.

On Wednesday's episode of "The Daily Show," host Josh Johnson pointed out a detail at Donald Trump Jr.'s wedding that looks like it came straight out of a very popular horror movie—and once you see it, you can't unsee it.

Johnson played a snippet of Trump sharing footage of his wedding to socialite Bettina Anderson to social media. The wedding was held on a small island in the Bahamas in May, and then dropped his hilarious punchline.

Set to an acoustic version of The Ronettes' "Be My Baby," the clip opens with an aerial shot of the church where the president's eldest son married, before showing interior shots of guests inside. Ivanka and Tiffany Trump, Don Jr.'s sisters, are seen seated in a pew before the footage cuts to slow-motion footage of the bride and groom embracing each other at the altar with a massive cross above them.

Johnson joked, "What a beautiful wedding at the church from Sinners," while showing a screenshot from the Oscar-winning film of Sammie (played by Miles Caton) walking into his father's church covered in blood. Above Sammie—also—like, just like Don Jr. and his bride—is a giant cross. The exterior of the church from Sinners also matches the exterior of the church in the Bahamas.

Donald Trump Jr.'s wedding earlier drew widespread attention, as ProPublica reported earlier this week that the wedding was paid for by Russian oligarch Umar Kremlev, who has close ties to President Vladimir Putin.

Amid the fallout, Bettina Anderson issued a statement on Instagram clarifying: "Don and I got married privately on Friday, with only family present."

She continued: "The weekend that followed had been planned long in advance, originally intended as a fun weekend with friends. It was never meant to be a wedding celebration. When our original wedding plans changed, we decided to get married earlier and attend the already-planned weekend as a newly married couple."

She also wrote that the couple's "dear friend Umar very generously hosted two wonderful nights of celebrations for our celebration after the wedding."

Johnson had a pretty hilarious response to Bettina Anderson's clarification as well.

Johnson, impersonating Bettina Anderson, said: "Yeah, right, fake news. They didn't pay for my wedding—they paid for an even more expensive after-party."
